title: Camavinga Refuses to Leave Real Madrid Despite Club Push and Premier League Interest
excerpt: The French midfielder is determined to prove himself under José Mourinho, even as Manchester United and other Premier League clubs circle for a potential transfer.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Eduardo Camavinga insists on staying at Real Madrid despite being labeled transferable.
  • Manchester United is interested but needs Camavinga's consent to proceed with a transfer.
  • Camavinga had a challenging 2025/26 season with only 23 starts in 43 appearances.
  • Real Madrid's pursuit of Rodri could limit Camavinga's playing time further.
  • Camavinga's contract runs until 2029, giving Real Madrid leverage in negotiations.
https://youtube.com/watch?v=iL345eg5Izw

Player Digs In as Club Opens the Door

Eduardo Camavinga is not going anywhere — at least not willingly. The 23-year-old French midfielder has made clear to Real Madrid that he intends to stay and fight for his place under new manager José Mourinho, even as the club actively shops him to Premier League suitors, sources told Managing Madrid this week.

https://x.com/premierleague/status/2080267684663767078

Real Madrid have labelled Camavinga a transferable player as they look to generate funds for further squad investment. The club signed Marc Cucurella from Chelsea for €60 million, Denzel Dumfries from Inter Milan, and secured Bernardo Silva on a free transfer from Manchester City this summer. To balance the books, Los Blancos need outgoings — and Camavinga is their most marketable surplus asset.

But the player's stance has created an impasse. "The message coming from Camavinga is that he wants to work under José Mourinho and try to revive his career at Real Madrid," transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano said. "If at some point something changes and Camavinga opens doors to an exit, for sure the Premier League is a very likely destination. But at the moment, the desire of Camavinga remains to stay."

A Season to Forget

Camavinga's determination comes after a bruising 2025/26 campaign. He made 43 appearances across all competitions but started just 23 matches, logging only 2,198 minutes — well below several teammates who surpassed the 4,000-minute mark. Only seven of those outings were for the full 90 minutes. Injuries sidelined him for nine games.

His output reflected the disruption: two goals and one assist in all competitions. France manager Didier Deschamps omitted him from the World Cup squad entirely, citing a "difficult season" in Madrid.

"The only way to get him is to get the green light from the player. And at the moment, the message coming from Camavinga is that he wants to work under José Mourinho."

— Fabrizio Romano, transfer journalist

Rather than sulk over the World Cup snub, Camavinga enrolled in a short course on sports, entertainment, and media business at Harvard Business School — a move that drew attention for its maturity but did little to quiet the transfer noise around him.

Manchester United Circle, but Cannot Force the Issue

Manchester United have been the most persistent suitors. Manager Michael Carrick needs midfield reinforcement after Casemiro's departure to Inter Miami and with Manuel Ugarte unlikely to be available until later in the season. According to Romano, United have held conversations with Camavinga's agents to gauge his availability and have internally discussed him as a serious midfield option.

Inter Milan and Manchester City have also been linked. City were offered the player directly by Real Madrid, according to OneFootball, while Spanish journalist Sergio Valentin reported that Los Blancos are prioritising a move for City's Rodri — a deal that, if completed, would further marginalize Camavinga in Mourinho's midfield pecking order.

As things stand, Camavinga sits behind Aurélien Tchouaméni and Federico Valverde in the rotation for Mourinho's preferred double pivot. His contract runs until 2029, giving Real Madrid leverage on price but no mechanism to force him out.

What Comes Next

The standoff has a clear timeline. With preseason under way and La Liga's opener against Espanyol approaching, Mourinho's early selections will reveal how much runway Camavinga truly has. The Portuguese manager has reportedly spoken to the player about the pecking order, though he has stopped short of directly asking him to leave.

Real Madrid are holding out for a premium fee — they will not sell cheaply a player who signed from Rennes in 2021 and has since accumulated 223 appearances, two La Liga titles, and two Champions League trophies. But with limited interest at that price point, Managing Madrid reports, the most likely outcome is that Camavinga stays and attempts to change minds on the training ground.

For the player, who turns 24 this winter, the next few weeks of preseason may define whether his Real Madrid career gets a second act or whether market realities eventually override personal resolve.
